taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: FEIS species review, Yucca baccata: leaf clusters are approximately 24 to 30 inches (60-75 cm) high and twice as wide.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: in flower up to about 1.5 m, the panicle within or a quarter beyond the rosette (FNA vol. 26 pp. 427-428, var. baccata); FNA gives the species, with its caulescent var. brevifolia, as shorter than 2.5 m. FEIS's 30 feet is not used.

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Yucca baccata: a native, perennial shrub.

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Yucca baccata: rhizomatous stems 8-15 cm in diameter, 20-55 cm long, covered with thick bark.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata var. baccata: plants acaulescent or caulescent; stems, if present, 1-6, aerial or subterranean, shorter than 0.3 m.

traits.clonal.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: plants often forming open colonies of rosettes; FEIS: 1 or 2 adventitious sprouts emerge from the upper surface of the rhizomes.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves live for years, as in every yucca.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: leaf blade erect, bluish green, concavo-convex, rigid.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Yucca baccata: individual blades reaching lengths of 20 to 40 inches (51-102 cm); FNA: 30-100 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: leaf blade 30-100 x 2-6 cm; FEIS: widths of 1.25 to 1.50 inches (3.2-3.8 cm).

traits.leaf_shape.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: blades long and narrow, about twenty times as long as wide: linear.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: leaf blade bluish green, scabrous or glaucous; olive to blue-green in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: inflorescences erect, paniculate, dense; FEIS: 11 to 18 flowering branches.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: inflorescences ovoid, 6-8.2 dm.

traits.peduncle_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata var. baccata: peduncle 0.6-0.8 m.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: FEIS species review, Yucca baccata: the panicle is 12 to 36 inches (30.5-91.4 cm) long with 11 to 18 flowering branches.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: tepals usually cream-colored, occasionally tinged with purple; sRGB by eye from the photos, where the buds show the purple.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: flowers pendent, 5-13 cm, nearly as wide.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: fruits pendent, baccate, indehiscent, elongate, fleshy, succulent.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: fruits 5-23 x 4-7.5 cm.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 p. 424, 427, 428 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Yucca baccata: fruits 5-23 x 4-7.5 cm.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 198, Yucca baccata: 3,000 to 8,000 feet, April to July; FEIS: flowering dates range from March to July, later at higher elevation.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: fruits ripe July to September.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for banana yucca from FEIS (Groen 2005) and Flora of North America vol. 26: rosettes 60-75 cm high of erect, rigid leaves 51-102 cm long (leaf_length 0.7, old_angle 42), stemless or with stems under 0.3 m in var. baccata (trunk_rate 0), open colonies from rhizomes (pups 4), a dense panicle of 11 to 18 branches within or a quarter beyond the rosette (stalk_height 1.0), pendent flowers 5-13 cm (flower_angle 100, flower_size 0.07). FEIS: a 3-year reproductive cycle is likely (bloom 0.35). Leaf rate and life are estimates.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: an open colony of stemless rosettes of stiff, erect, bluish to olive-green sword leaves edged with curling brown fibres, a dense panicle of pendent cream bells, purple-tinged in bud, held among or just above the leaves.

allometry.note: 0.8 m tall at 20 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
